title: Density versus probability
statement:
What does integrating |ψ|² over a region of space give for a normalized one-electron orbital?

[_]{a}

choices: The probability of finding the electron in that region
explanations: Integration converts density into a dimensionless probability.
A quantum orbital is not a specified trajectory.
That is not obtained from this integral alone.
A transition energy is needed for that.

hints: Summing density over a region produces a probability.
solution: |ψ|² is a density. Summing density over a region produces a probability. Whole-space integration equals one. Integration converts density into a dimensionless probability.
